column2: For them there is nothing to be done or left undone, no samadhi or final goal, no injunction or prohibition — just as with me.
Just as nothing remains to be accomplished for me, who am complete here, so it is for those who have fulfilled their purpose, without doubt.
For the good of my devotees they have taken on human nature; fallen from the world of Rudra, they are Rudras — there is no doubt of it.
Just as my command sets Brahma and the others in motion, so their direction sets other men in motion.
Through their being vessels of my command and their abundance of true feeling, by merely seeing them all sin is destroyed.
And signs appear, indicating excellent fruits, in men who have feeling for me, pertaining to things not seen before:
trembling, sweat, shedding of tears, change of voice in the throat, and sudden experiences of bliss and the like, again and again.
By these unfailing marks, singly or all together, in mild, middling or intense degree, those best of men are to be known.
Just as iron heated through by fire is no longer mere iron, so through my presence they are no longer mere men.
Because they have hands, feet and the rest like others, a wise man should not despise these Rudras bearing mortal bodies, taking them for ordinary people.
exposition, celibacy, hearing, austerity, forbearance, purity, the tuft and the sacred thread, the turban and the upper garment,
Contempt shown them by men of deluded mind robs them of life, fortune, family and character and brings them to hell.
Even the state of Brahma, Vishnu and the lord of the gods seems like a wisp of cotton to those great souls who are lifted up and depend on nothing but me.
The impure lordship of the intellect, of nature and of the Purusha belongs to the lords of the qualities; therefore it is to be given up by those who seek the state beyond the qualities.
What more need be said? The one means of attaining the highest good is attachment of the mind to me, by whatever cause.
Upamanyu said: Thus Shiva, the supreme self, lord Shrikantha, spoke for the good of the worlds this summary of the essence of knowledge.
The Vedas and shastras in their entirety, with the Itihasas and Puranas and all the sciences, are but the extended explanation of this summary of knowledge.
Knowledge, the knowable, what is to be practised, eligibility, the means and the goal — this summary is the summary of these six topics.
Knowledge belongs to the guru; the knowable is the bond, the bound soul and the Lord; what is to be practised is linga worship and the rest; and the eligible is the devotee.
The means are Shiva's mantras and the rest; the goal is equality with Shiva. Knowledge of this summary of six topics is called omniscience.
First, having worshipped Shiva outwardly with devotion by rites, sacrifices and the like according to one's wealth, one should then become devoted to the inner worship.
avoiding what is forbidden, wearing ash and rudraksha, worship on festival days, O Goddess, and especially on the fourteenth,
For the great soul whose delight is within and not in outward things, out of regard for merit, no outer rite need be performed.
For one satisfied with the nectar of knowledge, whose self is Shiva through devotion, there is never anything to be done, O Krishna, either within or without.
Therefore, gradually giving up the outer and then the inner, having seen the knowable through knowledge, one should give up knowledge too.
If the mind is not one-pointed on Shiva, what use are rites performed? If the mind is one-pointed, what use are rites performed?
Therefore, whether performing rites or not, in order, within and without, one should fix the mind on Shiva by whatever means.
For the good whose minds are fixed on Shiva and whose understanding is established, there is supreme peace here and hereafter and everywhere.
Here all accomplishments come through this mantra, "Om namah Shivaya"; therefore it is to be taken up for glory high and low.
drinking the brahmakurcha every month according to rule, and worshipping me especially after bathing me with it, dear one,
avoiding the food of all rites, avoiding food of the shraddha, likewise stale food, and barley gruel especially,
avoiding wine, what smells of wine, and food offered to other gods — this is common to all classes, and especially to brahmins.
Forbearance, peace, contentment, truth, not stealing, celibacy, knowledge of me, dispassion, the use of ash,
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 12: the description of the greatness of the five syllables. Shri Krishna said: Best of great sages, all-knowing ocean of all knowledge, I wish to hear truly the greatness of the five syllables.
It stands by its very nature in the relation of denoted and denoting: Shiva is the denoted, being immeasurable, and the mantra is remembered as what denotes him.
This relation of denoted and denoting between them is beginningless, just as this terrible ocean of worldly existence has flowed from beginningless time.
So too Shiva, beginningless, stands as the releaser from worldly existence; just as medicine is by nature the opponent of diseases,
so Shiva is remembered as the opponent of the faults of worldly existence. If this lord of the world did not exist, all this would become darkness,
since Prakriti is insentient and the Purusha ignorant. Primal matter, atoms and whatever else is insentient
are not seen to act by themselves without an intelligent cause. Instruction in dharma and adharma, bondage and liberation — upon reflection,
the first creation of men is not established without an all-knowing one; just as the sick suffer joylessly without a physician.
Therefore there exists the beginningless, all-knowing, perfect Sadashiva, the lord who delivers men from the ocean of worldly existence.
Free of beginning, middle and end, pure by nature, the lord, all-knowing and perfect — so Shiva is to be known in Shiva's Agama.
This mantra is his name, and he is remembered as what it names; because of this naming and named relation, the mantra is established as the supreme Shiva.
Upamanyu said: The greatness of the five syllables cannot be told in full even in hundreds of millions of years; therefore hear it in brief.
This much is the knowledge of Shiva, this much the supreme state: the six-syllabled word of Shiva, "Om namah Shivaya."
This Shaiva saying is an injunction, not mere praise; it is of the nature of Shiva. Shiva, who is all-knowing, perfect and pure by nature,
and who bestows grace on the worlds — how could he speak falsely? A thing as it is, with its merits and faults by nature,
and its full fruit, the all-knowing would tell as it is. One would speak falsely through being seized by faults such as passion and ignorance;
since these do not exist in the Lord, how could he speak otherwise? The pure word composed by Shiva, all-knowing and untouched by any fault, is authoritative; there is no doubt.
Therefore the words of the Lord concerning true merit and sin should be believed by the wise; one who disbelieves them goes down.
Whatever splendid word has been spoken by peaceful excellent sages for the attainment of heaven and liberation should be known as well spoken.
A word that follows passion, hatred, falsehood, anger, lust and craving is called ill spoken, since it leads to hell.
What use is it, even if refined, gentle or graceful — a word of ignorance and passion that causes the afflictions of worldly existence?
A word by hearing which welfare arises and passion and the rest are destroyed should be known as fine, even if it is misshapen.
This six-syllabled mantra, found in both the Veda and Shiva's Agama, accomplishes every aim for all devotees of Shiva.
Though there are many mantras, there is nowhere any equal to the pure mantra composed by the all-knowing Shiva.
The Vedas and shastras with their limbs are contained in the six syllables; therefore there is no other mantra anywhere equal to it.
The six-syllabled mantra is distinct from the seven crore great mantras and the many subsidiary mantras, as a sutra is from its commentary.
All the teachings of Shiva and all the branches of learning are, in brief, the commentary on the sutra of the six syllables.
What need of many mantras or very extensive shastras has he in whose heart this mantra "Om namah Shivaya" abides?
He has studied, he has heard, he has done and performed everything, who has made firm the practice of the mantra "Om namah Shivaya."
Fruitful is the life of him on the tip of whose tongue dwell the three syllables "Shivaya" joined with "namah" and the rest.
Whether outcaste or lowly, fool or scholar, one devoted to the japa of the five syllables is freed from the cage of sin.
So said the supreme Lord, the trident-bearer, when asked by the Goddess, for the good of all mortals, and of the twice-born especially.
That word, of few syllables yet rich in meaning, the essence of the Veda, giver of liberation, established by command, free of doubt, is of the nature of Shiva.
Endowed with many powers, divine, delighting the minds of people, of well-settled meaning and profound — such is the word of the supreme Lord.
For the accomplishment of every aim of all embodied beings, the all-knowing one declared the mantra "Om namah Shivaya," easy to utter.
That primal six-syllabled mantra is the seed of all learning; it is to be known as most subtle yet of great meaning, like the seed of the banyan.
The god beyond the three qualities, all-knowing, the lord who does all, Shiva the all-pervading, abides in the one-syllabled mantra "Om."
The subtle one-syllabled Brahmans beginning with Ishana abide in order in the mantra "namah Shivaya"; in the subtle six-syllabled mantra Shiva abides, whose body is the five Brahmans.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 13: the description of the greatness of the five syllables. The Goddess said: In the Kali age, a sullied time, hard to overcome and hard to escape, when the world is covered by the darkness of demerit and turned away from dharma,
If a fallen man, deluded, worships me with mantras but without my five syllables, he will go to hell, no doubt.
Those who live on water or on air and others emaciated by vows do not reach my world by these vows.
But whoever worships me even once with devotion using the five syllables alone goes to my abode, through the greatness of this mantra.
Therefore austerities, sacrifices, vows and observances are not equal to even a ten-millionth part of worship with the five syllables.
Whether bound or freed from the noose, whoever worships me with the five syllables is liberated; there is no need to deliberate on this.
Whether without Rudra's initiation or with it, whether fallen or foolish, the man who worships me even once with the five syllables is liberated.
With the six syllables, O Goddess, or with the five syllables, if one worships me devoutly with the Brahma-limbs, one is liberated.
Fallen or not fallen, one should worship with this mantra — my devotee who has conquered anger, whether he has received it from a guru or not.
One who has received it is ten million times greater than one who has not; therefore, O Goddess, one should receive it and then worship me with this mantra.
Whoever, having received it, worships me, endowed with friendliness and other virtues and devoted to celibacy, attains likeness to me through devotion.
when the conduct of classes and stages of life has decayed, when calamity is at hand, when all right to perform rites is in doubt or has been reversed,
What more need be said? All devotees are eligible for my five-syllabled mantra; therefore it is the most excellent.
By the power of the five syllables the worlds, the Vedas, the great sages, the eternal dharmas, the gods and this whole universe endure.
When the dissolution comes and all things moving and unmoving perish, everything returns to Prakriti and dissolves there.
I alone remain, O Goddess; there is no second anywhere. Then the Vedas and shastras all abide in the five syllables.
They do not perish, protected by my Shakti. Then creation arises from me through the division of Prakriti and the self,
and of the qualities, forms and selves; then comes the intermediate dissolution. Then the god Narayana, taking a body made of maya,
sleeps on the serpent couch in the midst of the waters; from the lotus of his navel is born the five-faced Grandsire,
who, wishing to create the three worlds but unable without help, first created ten lords of sages, mind-born and of boundless energy.
For the increase of their powers the Grandsire said to me: "Mahadeva, Maheshvara, give power to my sons."
Entreated thus by him, I, bearing five faces, spoke the five syllables in order to the lotus-born.
when teaching has been obstructed and the succession of guru and disciple has gone — by what means are your devotees liberated, Maheshvara?
Receiving them with his five faces, the Grandsire of the worlds knew me, Maheshvara, through the relation of denoted and denoting.
Having learned their use according to rule and mastered the mantra, Prajapati gave the mantra and its meaning truly to his sons.
They, having received the jewel of mantras directly from the Grandsire of the worlds, longing to worship me by the path he enjoined,
on the lovely peak of Meru is a mountain named Munjavat, ever dear to me, glorious, always guarded by my devotees —
near it, eager to create the world, they performed intense austerities for a thousand divine years, living on air.
Seeing their devotion, I at once became visible to them, and told those noble ones the seer, the metre, the pin, the seed, the power and the deity,
the placing, the six limbs, the binding of the directions and the application in full, for the creation and increase of the world.
Then those sages, by the greatness of the mantra and the strength of austerity, properly spread forth creation with gods, asuras and men.
Now the form of this supreme knowledge is told: first "namah" is to be used, and after it "Shivaya."
This is the five-syllabled knowledge, which reaches the crown of all the Shrutis, the eternal seed of all that has come into being.
The Lord said: Resorting to my supreme and lovely five-syllabled knowledge, and with selves cultivated by devotion, men born in the Kali age are liberated.
It first issued from my mouth and denotes me alone; she shines like molten gold, with full, high breasts,
four-armed, three-eyed, crowned with the young moon, holding lotus and water-lily, gentle, her hands showing the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures,
endowed with every auspicious mark, adorned with every ornament, seated on a white lotus, with dark curling hair.
Its letters are of five colours, with shining circles of rays: yellow, black, smoky, golden and red.
If these are used separately, adorned with bindu and nada — the bindu like a half-moon and the nada in the shape of a lamp-flame —
the second among the syllables is the seed of this mantra, O fair-faced one; one should declare the fourth, preceded by a long vowel, and the fifth as the power.
The seer is named Vamadeva, the metre is declared to be Pankti, and the deity of this mantra is I, Shiva, O fair-faced one.
Gautama, Atri, Vishvamitra, Angiras and Bharadvaja, O fair one, are remembered as the seers of the letters in order.
Gayatri, Anushtubh, Trishtubh, Brihati and Viraj are the metres, and Indra, Rudra, Hari, Brahma and Skanda their deities.
My five faces, O fair-faced one, are said to be their places, from the east to the upward one, beginning with na in order.
defiled by faults of mind, speech and body beyond telling or remembering — for the ungrateful, the slanderers, the deceitful,
The first letter is udatta, and the fourth and second too; the fifth is svarita, and the third is remembered as low.
Mulavidya, Shiva, Shaiva, Sutra and Panchakshara — one should know these as its names; it is my great Shaiva heart.
The letter na is called the head, ma the tuft, shi the armour, va is called the eye,
and ya the weapon; namah, svaha, vashat, hum, vaushat and phat at the end of the letters make them limbs.
There too this is the root mantra, with a slight difference in combination; there too the fifth letter is adorned with the twelfth vowel.
Therefore with this mantra, through mind, speech and body, one should perform our worship, and japa, fire offering and the like,
according to one's understanding, time, the shastra, one's mind, strength, means, fitness and delight.
Whenever and wherever performed with devotion, and by whomever, O Goddess, the worship will lead to liberation.
Whatever is done for me with a mind attached to me, lovely one, is dear to me and auspicious, whether in due order or out of order.
Still, for those devotees of mine who are not utterly helpless, I myself have laid down the rule in all the shastras.
for the greedy and crooked-minded, yet turned toward me — my five-syllabled knowledge carries them across the fear of worldly existence.
There, first, I shall tell of the auspicious receiving of the mantra, without which japa is fruitless and by which it becomes fruitful.
Thus, O Goddess, I have again and again made the promise on earth: even a fallen devotee of mine is liberated by this knowledge.
The Goddess said: If a mortal is fallen, he becomes wholly unfit for rites; and a rite done by one unfit leads to hell. How then is a fallen man liberated by this knowledge?
The Lord said: What you say is true; yet hear, lovely one, this which I kept hidden before, regarding it as a secret.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 14: the description of the glory of the five syllables. The Lord said: Japa without command, without rite, without faith, O fair-faced one, and without the fee for the command, is always fruitless.
Having bathed him for purification with ghee from a full pot, and with water purified by mantras and mixed with holy substances,
having adorned him well with fragrance, garlands, garments and ornaments, having the auspicious day proclaimed and honouring brahmins,
on the seashore, by a river, in a cowpen or a temple, in a clean place or at home, at a time and on a lunar day that brings success,
under an auspicious star and conjunction free of all faults, favouring him, the guru should give him my knowledge according to rule.
In solitude, very serene of mind, he should utter it properly with its tone; having uttered our excellent mantra and had him utter it,
saying "May it be auspicious, may it be good, may it be splendid, may it be dear," thus the guru should give the mantra, and after that the command.
Having thus received the mantra and command from the guru, collected, he should make the resolve and recite it daily, preceded by the preparatory rite.
As long as he lives he should recite it daily one thousand and eight times; single-minded and devoted, he goes to the supreme goal.
He should respectfully recite it a hundred thousand times per syllable, multiplied by four; eating only at night and self-restrained, he is remembered as one who has done the preparatory rite.
Whoever, having performed the preparatory rite, then recites it daily has no equal in the world; he is perfected and becomes a giver of perfection.
Established by command, by rite and by faith, of my nature — if it is thus, with the fee, the mantra's perfection brings great fruit.
Having bathed, in a clean place, taking a pleasant seat, thinking in his heart of me with you, and then thinking of his own guru,
facing north or east, silent and one-pointed in mind, purifying the five elements by burning, flooding and the like,
having performed the placing of the mantra and the rest, his body made fruitful, meditating on our two forms and restraining prana and apana,
remembering the seat of knowledge, its own form, the seer, metre, presiding deity, seed, power and the sentence, he should recite the five syllables.
Those versed in the meaning of the Agamas say that mental japa is the best, whispered japa the middling, and spoken japa the lowest.
They say in order that the best has Rudra as its deity, the middling Vishnu, and the lowest Brahma.
When one utters the mantra aloud with high, low and circumflex tones, with words and syllables clear or unclear, this is remembered as spoken japa.
When it is barely uttered, with only a movement of the tongue, unheard by others or only slightly heard, it is called whispered.
When with the mind, along the row of syllables, from letter to letter and word to word, one reflects again and again on the sound and its meaning, it is called mental japa.
The spoken is counted as one, the whispered is said to be a hundred, the mental a thousand, and that with breath-control more than a hundred times more.
Approaching a guru, a brahmin, a teacher who knows the truth, a reciter endowed with good qualities and devoted to the yoga of meditation,
Japa joined with breath-control is called sagarbha; even without it, breath-control at the beginning and end is praised.
The wise one who knows the meaning of the mantra should restrain the breath and remember the mantra forty times; if unable, he should recite according to his strength.
He should practise breath-control five times, three times or once, without mantra or with mantra; with mantra is praised there.
Japa with meditation is said to be a thousand times greater even than sagarbha; of these five kinds, one should practise one according to one's ability.
Counting japa on the finger is declared to be onefold; by lines, know it to be eightfold; with putrajiva seeds, tenfold more;
with conch beads a hundredfold, with coral a thousandfold, with crystal ten thousandfold, and with pearls it is said to be a hundred thousandfold;
with lotus seeds a million-fold, and with gold ten million-fold; with knots of kusha and with rudraksha it becomes infinitely multiplied.
A rosary made of thirty beads gives wealth in the practice of japa; one of twenty-seven beads gives prosperity;
one made of twenty-five gives liberation; and one of fifteen beads gives the fruit of hostile magic.
Know that the thumb gives liberation, the forefinger destroys enemies, the middle finger gives wealth, and the ring finger brings peace.
one should please him diligently, endowed with purity of feeling, by speech, mind, body and wealth.
A rosary of a hundred and eight is the very best, one of a hundred is excellent, and one of fifty is middling.
One of fifty-four beads is declared best for the heart. Thus one should do japa with a rosary, and show it to no one.
The little finger is called the dripping one and is fine in japa; one should recite with the thumb together with the other fingers,
since japa done without the thumb is fruitless. Japa at home should be known as of equal value; in a cowpen, they know it as a hundredfold;
in a holy forest or a garden it is said to be a thousandfold; on a holy mountain ten thousandfold; by a river it is declared a hundred thousandfold;
in a temple they say ten millionfold, and in my presence infinite. In the presence of the sun, fire, guru, moon, a lamp or water,
of brahmins or of cows, japa is praised. Facing east it brings control; facing south it is for hostile magic;
know that facing west it gives wealth, and facing north it gives peace. In the presence of the sun, fire, brahmins, gods and gurus,
and of others engaged in it, one should not recite the mantra with face turned away. Wearing a turban, a jacket, naked, with loose hair, with the neck covered,
with impure hands, unclean or lamenting, one should never do japa. Anger, intoxication, sneezing — these three, spitting and yawning,
The brahmin should always worship the teacher with great effort; elephants, horses, chariots, jewels, fields and houses,
and the sight of dogs and lowly people should be avoided in japa. If these occur, one should sip water, or remember me together with you,
or look at the luminaries, or practise breath-control. Without a seat, lying down, walking or standing,
in a street, in an inauspicious place, or in darkness one should not do japa; nor with legs stretched out, nor in the cock posture,
nor mounted on a vehicle or bed, nor distracted by worry. If able, one should observe all this; if unable, recite as one can.
What more need be said? Hear the word in brief: one of good conduct who recites purely and meditates attains the good.
Good conduct is the highest dharma, good conduct the highest wealth, good conduct the highest learning, good conduct the highest goal.
A man without good conduct is reviled in the world and will not be happy hereafter; therefore one should be of good conduct.
Whatever duty is enjoined for each person in the Veda and the shastras by the Vedic authorities — practising that is good conduct, and not otherwise.
Because it is practised by the good it is called good conduct; they say that faith is the root cause of that good conduct.
If a man of faith, through negligence and the like, does not stray from good conduct, he is never defiled; therefore one should cultivate faith.
ornaments, garments, grain and wealth — these one should give to the guru with devotion, when one has the means.
The conviction that, just as there is happiness and sorrow here through good and evil deeds, so there is hereafter, is called faith.
I shall tell another secret, which is to be guarded, dear one; it is not to be told to anyone, nor to an unbeliever or a bound soul.
For one without good conduct, for the fallen and the outcaste, there is no protection in the Kali age beyond the five syllables.
Whether walking or standing or acting at will, whether impure or pure, this mantra is never fruitless.
For men without good conduct, whose six paths are unpurified, even if not given by a guru, this mantra is never fruitless.
For the outcaste, the fool, the deluded, the fallen, the lawless and the lowly, this mantra is never fruitless.
For one devoted to me, even in every condition, it surely succeeds, without doubt; but not for anyone else.
For this mantra, dear one, the ascendant, lunar day, star, weekday, conjunction and the like need not be closely examined; it is never asleep, but always awake.
This great mantra is never anyone's enemy; it is either well perfected, perfected, or to be perfected.
Taught by a perfected guru it is called well perfected; given even by an unperfected one, it is simply perfected or to be perfected.
If one desires success for oneself, one should not be niggardly with wealth; then, having offered oneself with one's belongings to the guru,
Whether practised or not, it succeeds, no doubt, for one endowed with abundant faith in me, in the mantra and in the guru.
Therefore, giving up other mantras, which are beset with obstacles because of eligibility, the wise man should take refuge in the supreme knowledge, the five syllables themselves.
When other mantras are perfected, this mantra is not thereby perfected; but when this great mantra is perfected, they too become perfected.
Just as I am not obtained when the gods are obtained, O great queen, but when I am obtained they are obtained, the same rule holds among these mantras.
The faults of all other mantras cannot arise in this one, since this mantra works without regard to caste and the like.
Even so, one should not rashly apply it to petty or hostile ends; for this is very mighty.
Upamanyu said: Thus Mahadeva the trident-bearer himself told the great Goddess, for the good of the worlds, the rite of the five syllables as it is.
Whoever recites this with devotion or hears it with a collected mind is freed from all sins and goes to the supreme goal.
having thus worshipped him properly according to one's means without deceit, one should receive from the guru the mantra and the knowledge in due order.
The guru, thus pleased with the disciple who has worshipped him and lived with him a year, who is obedient, free of ego, bathed, pure and fasting,
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 15: the description of the greatness of the guru in the rite of initiation. Shri Krishna said: Lord, you have told the greatness of the mantra and the rite of its use, like the Shruti itself.
The Shakti initiation, which consists of knowledge, is performed by the guru entering the disciple's body by the path of yoga with the eye of knowledge.
The mantra initiation, which consists of ritual action, preceded by fire-pit and mandala, is to be performed outwardly by the guru for those of dull and duller capacity.
The disciple deserves grace according to the descent of Shakti, since in brief the following of Shaiva dharma is rooted in it.
Where Shakti has not descended, purification does not arise — neither knowledge, nor Shaiva conduct, nor liberation, nor powers.
Therefore, observing the signs of an abundant descent of Shakti, the guru should purify the disciple by knowledge or by ritual.
The foolish one who does otherwise out of delusion perishes; therefore the guru should examine the disciple in every way.
The mark of the descent of Shakti is the arising of awakening and bliss, since that supreme Shakti is of the nature of awakening and bliss.
The sign of bliss and awakening is a change in the inner faculties, as when there are trembling, horripilation and changes in voice, eyes and limbs.
The disciple too should test the guru by these marks, through contact with him in Shiva's worship and the like, whether met there or belonging to him.
The disciple, being one to be taught, should hold the guru in reverence; therefore he should show reverence to the guru with every effort.
Now I wish to hear of the excellent Shaiva sacrament; something was indicated in the receiving of the mantra, and I have not forgotten it.
He who is the guru is declared to be Shiva, and he who is Shiva is remembered as the guru; the guru is Shiva himself, abiding in the form of knowledge.
As Shiva is, so is knowledge; as knowledge is, so is the guru; the worship of Shiva, of knowledge and of gurus bears equal fruit.
The guru embodies all gods and is made of all mantras; therefore one should bear his command on one's head with every effort.
One who seeks welfare should not transgress the guru's command even in mind, since one who keeps the guru's command attains the wealth of knowledge.
Walking, standing, sleeping or eating, he should not undertake any other act; if he does anything in his presence, he should do it all with the guru's permission.
In the guru's house or in his presence he should not sit as he pleases, since the guru is god in person and his house is a temple.
Just as one falls through the sin of associating with sinners, and just as gold casts off impurity through contact with fire, so a man casts off sin through contact with the guru.
As a pot of ghee placed near fire melts, so sin melts in the proximity of the teacher.
As a blazing fire burns both dry and wet, so the guru, when pleased, burns sin in an instant.
By mind, deed or word one should not cause the guru to be angry.
Upamanyu said: Ah, I shall tell you of the supreme, holy sacrament spoken by Shiva the Lord, which purifies all sins.
By his anger life, fortune, knowledge and good deeds are burned; the sacrifices of those who make him angry are fruitless,
and so are their restraints and observances; there is no need to deliberate on this. A man should never speak a word opposed to the guru;
if in great delusion he speaks one, he goes to the Raurava hell. By mind, deed and word, with regard to the guru, carefully,
the wise man seeking welfare should not behave falsely. He should always do what is good and pleasing to the guru, whether directed or not.
Whether in his presence or not, he should do his work. A devotee of such conduct, his mind always diligent,
a disciple who pleases his guru, then becomes worthy of the Shaiva dharmas. If the guru is virtuous and wise, revealing supreme bliss,
knowing the truth and devoted to Shiva, he gives liberation, and no other. The truth is what produces awareness and gives rise to supreme bliss;
he who has known that truth alone reveals bliss, not one who is a guru in name only, devoid of awareness.
Boats may carry one another across, but can a stone carry a stone across? By such a guru in name only, liberation is in name only.
Those who have known the truth are liberated and liberate others too. In one without the truth, whence understanding, whence the grasp of the self?
Since by it a man becomes properly qualified for worship and the rest, the sacrament is called the purification of the six paths.
One devoid of that grasp is called a bound soul; and one guided by bound souls does not pass beyond bondage.
Therefore only a knower of the truth is accepted here as liberated and a liberator. Though endowed with every mark and knowing all the shastras,
and knowing the rules of all means, one without the truth is fruitless. He whose understanding engages with the truth up to direct experience —
by his glance and the rest supreme bliss arises. Therefore, from contact with whom awakening and bliss arise,
him alone the wise man should choose as guru, and no other. That guru, honoured by disciples skilled in humility and conduct,
should be served by seekers of liberation until he is understood; when he is understood, devotion should be steady until one takes refuge in the truth.
One should never abandon the truth nor neglect it in any way. Where neither bliss nor awakening is found even slightly,

even after a year, the disciple should take refuge in another guru; even after going to another guru, he should not despise the former one, nor the guru's brothers, sons, teachers or those who urged him on.
There, first approaching a brahmin versed in the Veda, he should worship the guru, wise, auspicious and pleasing to behold,
the giver of all fearlessness, his mind filled with compassion; he should please him diligently by mind, deed and word.
Since by it knowledge is given and the bondage of the noose is destroyed, this sacrament is also called diksha.
The disciple should worship him until he is pleased; when he is pleased, the disciple's sin is at once destroyed.
Therefore wealth, jewels, fields and houses, ornaments and garments, vehicles, beds and seats —
these he should give to the guru with devotion according to his means; he should not be niggardly with wealth if he desires the supreme goal.
He alone is father, mother, husband, kinsman, wealth, happiness, companion and friend; therefore he should offer everything to him.
Having offered all, then offering himself with his family and possessions, with water, he should always be subject to him.
When an embodied being has given himself to Shiva in the form of the teacher, then he becomes a Shaiva, and for him there is no rebirth.
The guru should examine the disciple who has come to him for one year if a brahmin, two years if a kshatriya, three if a vaishya,
by demands for life and wealth and the like, and by fitting and unfitting commands — setting the excellent to low tasks and the low to excellent tasks.
Those who, though abused or beaten, do not become despondent — they are fit, restrained and pure for the rite of the Shaiva sacrament.

upright, gentle, pure, humble, steady in mind, endowed with purity and good conduct, twice-born devotees of Shiva —
such people, endowed with such conduct in speech, mind, body and deed, are to be purified and awakened as is right; such is the conclusion of the shastras.
A woman has no right of her own to the Shaiva sacrament; she has it at her husband's direction, if she is devoted to the Lord.
Likewise one without a husband has the right with the permission of her son and others, and a maiden with her father's command. For shudras, mixed castes and the fallen especially,
and likewise for those of mixed birth, the purification of the paths is not prescribed; if they too have unfeigned feeling for Shiva, the supreme cause,
they should purify their sin by the gift of water from the guru's feet and the like. Those born in the direct order are joined with the twice-born;
for them the purification of the paths and the rest should be done as befits the mother's family. A maiden who has been directed to Shiva's dharma by her father and others
should be given to a devotee, not to another who is hostile. If through negligence she has been given to one opposed, she should enlighten her husband;
if unable, she should give him up in mind and practise dharma — as the chaste Anasuya, leaving her husband Atri, the excellent sage,
became fulfilled long ago by worshipping Shankara with austerity; as the Pandavas did by worshipping the god Narayana with austerity.
By the mere glance of the guru, by his touch or even by his conversation, awareness at once arises in a creature, destroying the noose.
She who, not directed by her elders, has found dharma herself — the fault arising from lack of independence does not in truth apply here,
for one directed to Shiva's dharma, out of reverence for Shiva's command. What more need be said? Whoever takes refuge in Shiva
is to be given the sacrament, if dependent on a guru; the sacrament does not differ. By the mere glance of the guru, by his touch or conversation,
for one in whom wisdom arises there is no defeat. The sacrament performed by the mind through the path of yoga
is secret and is not told here; it is known only from the guru's mouth. The sacrament with ritual action, preceded by fire-pit and pavilion, will be told in brief; it cannot be told at length.
That initiation is called Shambhavi, and it is again divided in two, intense and more intense, by the difference in the destruction of the noose.
That by which release comes at once is held to be the more intense; the intense purifies the man of sin utterly while he lives.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, book 7, part 2, chapter 16: the description of the sacrament of the disciple. Upamanyu said: On a holy day, in a clean place free of many faults, the teacher should first perform the sacrament called samaya.
On a bed of rice, husked grain, mustard, sesame, flowers and kusha, he should prepare there a Shiva pot bearing the proper marks,
of gold, silver, copper or clay, strewn with fragrance, flowers and unbroken grains, adorned with kusha and durva shoots,
wound with white thread at the neck, covered with a pair of new cloths, filled with pure water, with a kusha tuft, with substances and a lid.
A ewer, a vardhani vessel, a conch or a discus, and everything without thread and the like, or else a lotus leaf,
he should place on the northern petal of that lotus seat, and in front, with sandal-water, the vardhani of the king of weapons.
Then to the east of the mandala, and in the mantra pot as before, he should perform the great worship of the Lord according to rule.
